title: How much should you have saved by 30, 40, 50?

scenes.text: How much money should you have saved by 30? Most people guess way too low.
The rule of thumb: one year of salary by 30. Three times by 40. Six times by 50. Eight times by 60. And ten times your salary by 67.
If that made you feel sick, you're not alone. Mike is 35, and he's barely started.
Here's the fix. Save 15% of your pay, starting today. At 7% a year, Mike could still reach $1,071,000 by 67.
But Jake started the same plan at 25. He'll have $2,282,000. Those 10 years cost Mike over $1.2 million.
Behind? Don't panic. Start with whatever you can today, and raise it every year.
Comment your age, and tell me: are you on track?

props.disclaimer: Fidelity rule of thumb. Example: $60K salary, 15% saved, ~7% yearly return, not inflation-adjusted. Not financial advice.
